_comment: SE23 — the Tether Relay Station, spec §3 Band 3 and §32 rung 3. What STANDS at the relay, read by scripts/world/tether_relay.gd. The first mini-stronghold: a natural site partly industrialised, a compact traversal-and-combat site, and the moment Team Tether stops being something Grandpa described. Deliberately NOT everything about the place — the people on it are data/config/relay_site.json and data/config/trainers.json (SE25/SE27), the drained ground is terrain_playground.json's `drains` block, and the named region on the map is map_landmarks.json. Each of those files already owns its kind of thing. ALL POSITIONS AND SIZES TUNABLE.
_comment_site: The site coordinate is ADOPTED, not chosen. data/config/relay_site.json (SE25/SE27) picked [108,34] on the Old Quarry's own conduit bearing toward the stronghold and asked SE23 in writing to adopt it rather than name a second one. If the site ever moves, it moves THERE and here together, along with the four trainer positions derived from it.

site._frame: Everything below is authored in the site's OWN frame: `s` runs along the approach bearing (positive = deeper in, the direction the conduits already walk toward the stronghold), `t` runs across it, both in metres. tether_relay.gd converts with u = (0.565,-0.826) and p = (-u.z, u.x). Authoring in world XZ instead would make every tuning nudge a two-number trigonometry problem, and the five people SE25/SE27 stood up here are all within 1m of t=0 — the road IS the axis, so the axis is the frame.
site._ground: Probed with the real heightfield (tools/_probe_relay_site.gd). The site is a gentle south-east-facing shoulder: ground runs -5.6m at s=-24 up to -1.0m at s=+20, about 6 degrees along the approach, with a further ~2m fall toward +t. Nothing here needed a terrain flat; every wall, leg and pad is seated on its own sampled ground.
site._comment_weathering: ROUND7 MATERIAL DEFECT (ralph/reports/visual-parity/PLACES/round7/relay-before/06-relay-road-day.png). The compound's walls/gate/ramp were `severed_spokes.gd::_stone_material()` -- T_UnevenBrick under a StandardMaterial3D with NO `albedo_color` set at all, i.e. an implicit WHITE (1,1,1) tint. Under this site's own strong daylight key that bleached every sun-facing stone face to near-white (measured RGB(195.6,191.4,163.6) on the ground; the walls/gate/ramp read the same way) -- exactly the 'uniform clean stone'/'pale cream' defect `stronghold.gd`'s own VP8/VP8-EXT passes already fixed for the Hall with `hall_stone.gdshader` and a real darkened/desaturated `site.weathering` tint. `tether_relay.gd::_weathered_stone_material()` gives the relay's own walls/gate-piers/gate-lintel/ramp that same shader, reusing the identical installed T_UnevenBrick textures `severed_spokes.gd` already preloads (no new texture) and this site's OWN numbers below rather than the Hall's -- a smaller, closer-range compound than the Hall's towers wants a shallower damp band and less moss. `tile` 3.2 matches `severed_spokes.gd::STONE_TILE` (the value the rest of this site's untouched stone -- decks, apparatus massing -- still tiles at) so switching only the walls/gate/ramp to the shader does not visibly re-scale the brick course against the stone next to it. Cached ONCE (`_weathered_stone_material()`'s own cache), shared by every wall run, both gate piers, the lintel and every ramp slab -- one ShaderMaterial resource, not one per mesh, so batching is unaffected.

weathering._comment_base_tint: The stone's un-weathered value before darken/desaturate -- a light warm grey-tan, the same family `building_prefabs.json`'s LightRock/DarkRock retints use for this same kit elsewhere. TUNABLE.
weathering._comment_darken_desaturate: Same mechanism as `stronghold.json`'s `site.weathering.exterior` (darken 0.74, desaturate 0.5 there), tuned lighter here: the Hall is a distant ruin meant to read as a dark mass at 400m, the relay is a working compound the player stands inside of at 2-10m and a stone this dark would go flat/black under the same strong sun that bleached it white before. 0.5/0.4 is the middle of that band -- weathered, not blackened.
weathering._comment_moss_damp: Lower than the Hall's defaults (0.7/0.9/4.0/0.4/0.22): these walls are 2.6-7.2m of RECENT industrial masonry (this site's own header: 'a natural site partly industrialised'), not a centuries-ruined castle -- some weathering so the stone reads as real quarried rock instead of the old flat white, not the Hall's full overgrowth.
weathering._comment_tile: Matches `severed_spokes.gd::STONE_TILE` (3.2), the tiling the rest of this site's untouched stone -- decks, ramps' own collider mesh, the apparatus placeholder massing -- already carries, so the switch to the shader does not visibly re-scale the brick course.

_comment_walls: The compound. Team Tether's own masonry grammar, borrowed wholesale from severed_spokes.gd (`_ground_wall`, the stone material, the oxblood faction accent) rather than reimplemented — D24's 'one prop family' applied to the faction's buildings the same way the pylons already apply it to its hardware. PARTLY industrialised is the brief, so this is not a sealed box: a real wall across the approach face with the gate in it, flanks running back to enclose the yard, and an OPEN back where the compound simply gives out onto the drained ground. The player is meant to arrive at a front door, not to be locked in a room.

walls._why: the approach face, west of the gate opening; its inner end is the gate's own west pier
lower than the front: a yard fence, not a rampart. It also passes under the west conduit run, which is the read — the wall was built around hardware that was already here.

_comment_gate: OPEN, and that is the whole difference between this and the sealed gates on the severed spokes. A spoke gate's shut leaves are the message there; here the message is that Team Tether does not expect anyone to walk up this road, so the road runs straight through. Piers, a lintel and the faction colour on the lintel band; no leaves, nothing to unlock, no prompt.
_comment_decks: The traversal. The apparatus pad stands clear of the yard on solid legs, so the console is NOT reachable by walking at it — the player takes the ramp off the yard's west side, crosses the gantry, and steps onto the pad. That is the whole 'compact traversal challenge' the item asks for, and it is deliberately small: a mini-stronghold, not a dungeon (SD17 owns the dungeon). Deck heights are ABSOLUTE world Y, not heights above ground, because a walkway whose pieces each floated over their own sampled ground would step up and down along its length. OW5E: re-probed against the real corridor terrain (tools probe, not committed) after OW5D's own relay_site.json admitted ground truth at the new (350,3760) centre was never re-checked -- the old numbers (yard -4.6 to -2.2, deck at +0.1) described the PRE-corridor site at (108,34) and left the deck sitting 2-8m UNDER the new site's actual ground (which runs roughly 2.3m at the pad's south flank up to 8.0m at the yard's NW corner, a gentle south-east-facing shoulder, not a flat pad). `tests/smoke_relay_station.gd` caught it directly: the player could walk onto the 'raised' pad from the yard because the yard was higher than the platform. Deck now at +10.0 -- comfortably above every sampled point within 15m of the pad (max 6.92) and still only a ~20-degree climb from the ramp foot's own ground (~6.7), well inside the 45-degree floor_max_angle this file's own ramp comment already budgets for.

decks._comment_legs: EAST END ONLY. Which corners get a leg, in the deck's own signed frame. The gantry's west end is where the ramp arrives and a leg there stands inside the ramp's own 3.2m width — a pillar in the middle of the only route to the console. The smoke test found that on the first build (the player climbed to within a metre of the deck and stopped) and this is the fix; the west end is carried by the ramp structure it butts into.
decks._why: the walkway between the ramp head and the pad; 3.2m wide, which is comfortably walkable with a controller and still reads as industrial catwalk rather than as a road. Held well off the road axis (every one of SE25/SE27's five people stands within 1m of t=0) so the yard the fights happen in is clear floor.
the apparatus pad itself — the grounding base of the hero object, and the floor the console stands on. Abuts the gantry's east end at s=+2, so the two decks read as one raised level.

_comment_ramps: One ramp, run diagonally so it is long enough to be gentle: 9.6m of run for ~3.3m of rise (OW5E: re-probed against the real corridor terrain, foot ground ~6.7) is about 20 degrees, well inside the player's 45-degree floor_max_angle with room for the framerate to wobble. A ramp at the limit is a ramp that sometimes refuses, and this is the ONLY route to the console. Its head lands on the gantry's west end rather than beside it.
_comment_apparatus:
*** THE SEAM FOR THE HERO ASSET. READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING THE MASSING BELOW. ***

`docs/art/reference/14_Relay_Apparatus.png` is the owner-supplied board for this object (2026-08-11, labelled Band 3, drawn for exactly this item). It is one of the THREE hero objects D24 reserves Meshy for, alongside the Tether Energy Pylon (already generated, SF33) and the Legendary Tether Machine. The generation itself is a separate, OWNER-GATED task in the `art` lane and was NOT done here: this build had no Meshy access, and CLAUDE.md's rule is that a hero object is not improvised from scratch as if it were the final asset.

What stands here instead is a PLACEHOLDER MASSING, built from primitives wearing the materials severed_spokes.gd already defines (the medieval stone sheet, the oxblood faction accent, the reserved tether teal). It is laid out as the board's own five labelled subassemblies, in the board's own order, so that when the GLB lands the swap is one-for-one and each generated part has exactly one thing here to replace:

  grounding_base    the plinth and its splayed feet
  tether_core       the central column
  conductor_ring    the rings around it (the board's 'core and rings serviceable')
  conductor_arms    the arms out to the manifolds ('conductor arms ... replaceable')
  output_manifolds  the boxes the conduit runs land on
  console           the control console — the thing the player disables

HOW TO DO THE SWAP. tether_relay.gd::_build_apparatus is the only reader of this block; every subassembly it builds is a child of the `ApparatusSeam` node and nothing outside that node depends on any of them EXCEPT the console, which is found by name (`Console`) and carries the interactable. Drop the generated scene in as `ApparatusSeam`'s single child, keep a node named `Console` on it at roughly the console's authored position, delete the `massing` block below, and nothing else in the codebase has to change.

console._why_here: on the pad's western edge, facing back down the gantry — so it is the first thing on the pad the player meets after the crossing, and it is legible (a teal face on a pad of stone and oxblood) from the gantry's far end. Clear of the grounding base, whose 3.4m plinth starts at s=+3.6.
console.label: Disable the relay console
console._comment_flag: SB9's flat flag store (autoload/progression_state.gd). One-way: once set, the prompt goes away and the conduits stay dead across a save/load, because the flag is what the state is read from, not the node.
console._comment_requires_flag: SEAM FOR SE25 -- CLOSED 2026-08-22 (gates-abc-verification): SE25 has landed, `relay_captain` is in data/config/bands/band3_the_river_lock/trainers.json with defeat_flag `relay_captain_defeated`, and encounter_director.gd sets it on a real win, so the gate below is now live rather than empty. objectives.json already orders the beats defeat_the_relay_captain -> rescue_the_captive -> disable_the_relay, and the captive half was ALREADY gated on this flag (data/config/relay_site.json) -- only the console was still open, so the player could shut the relay down without ever meeting the captain. Original note follows. SEAM FOR SE25. Set this to `relay_captain_defeated` — the flag data/config/trainers.json's `relay_captain` sets — once SE25 has landed, and the console will refuse until the captain is beaten. Left EMPTY on purpose while SE25 is unmerged: a gate on a flag that nothing in this branch can set is a station the player cannot finish. The mechanism is built and tested (tests/smoke_relay.gd sets it and checks the refusal), only the value is waiting.
console.refused_message: The console is live and guarded. Whoever is running this station is still standing.
console.done_message: The relay goes quiet. Every conduit on the site dies with it.

apparatus._comment_seam_closed: SEAM CLOSED 2026-08-16. The owner authorised the generation and the key came from the Ralph art-lane Routine. Meshy multi-image-to-3D, refine tier, from the FRONT/SIDE/REAR crops of board 14 cut by tools/art_pipeline/crop_prop_views.py. The hero render on that board is deliberately not among the inputs: its callout numbers and leader lines sit on the object itself. `height` is the object's real size in metres -- board 14's own scale guide stands a figure at roughly its shoulder -- and tether_relay.gd fits the mesh to it by the mesh's own visual bounds rather than trusting its exported transform. The `massing` block below is NOT dead: it is the fallback the code still takes whenever `model` is empty or the file is missing, and it is the record of the five subassemblies the board names.

_comment_conduits:
Three runs converging on the pad, on SF33's Tether Energy Pylon and its sagging conduit spans — the same builder old_quarry.gd already borrows, for the same reason (see that file's header: a second implementation would be a second set of the same bugs). The story they tell is the point of the whole site. At the quarry, one line of lit pylons walks away over a hill. Here, three of them ARRIVE, and something is standing at the end of them. Every pylon is lit until the console goes off.

Height is 6.4 rather than the quarry's 4.6 so the spans clear the gantry deck: a cable strung at the shorter height would pass UNDER a walkway 2.8m over the ground, which reads as a broken prop rather than as infrastructure the compound was built around.

conduits._comment_cable_style: FIX 1 (code-blind judge pass, this branch): 'the glowing cyan cable arcs read as unanchored debug lines at the relay pylons.' `severed_spokes.gd`'s shared lit-conduit material/radius (CONDUIT_RADIUS 0.055, emission_energy_multiplier 0.8 -- that file is out of this lane's edit scope, and its material is cached by IDENTITY across every site that borrows it, quarry and spokes included, so it cannot be tuned in place without dimming those too) is duplicated PER RELAY SEGMENT instead: `tether_relay.gd::_dim_conduit_segments` walks every span this file draws, shrinks its own private `CylinderMesh`'s radius from the shared 0.055 to `cable_radius` below, and swaps a per-instance `material_override` (a dup of the shared lit material with `emission_energy_multiplier` dropped to `cable_emission_energy`) onto it. The dup is never installed as the segment's OWN `mesh.material` -- that field stays the real shared `_conduit_material(true)` untouched, which is what `_kill_the_conduits()`'s identity sweep still matches to swap every one of these to the shared dead material the moment the console is pressed.
conduits._comment_cable_radius: Was the shared default 0.055 (severed_spokes.gd's CONDUIT_RADIUS). 0.03 reads as a real cable rather than a drawn tube at the distances these shots stand at. TUNABLE.
conduits._comment_cable_emission_energy: Was the shared default 0.8 (severed_spokes.gd's own `emission_energy_multiplier`, tuned for the quarry's long receding pylon line). 0.4 halves it -- a live cable seen up close at the relay, not a line meant to read from 50m off. TUNABLE.

runs._why: the run in from the approach side — the same bearing the quarry's own line left on. This is the line the player has been following since Band 2, and it ends here.
in from the east flank, crossing the wall line — the compound was built around hardware that was already standing

_comment_cable_links: E-relay-dress (this pass): each conduit run above stops at its own LAST authored pylon -- west_run ends at local (0.5,-14.5), east_run at (14.5,-9), south_run at (6,-16.5) -- all 7-8m short of the apparatus centre at (7,-9). The runs converge ON the site but never actually touch the object they power, which is exactly the 'bare concrete slabs and pylons with nobody there' gap the render caught: cables that stop short read as floating hardware, not as infrastructure feeding a machine. `tether_relay.gd::_build_cable_links` adds one more sagged span per listed run, from that run's own last pylon's real top-frame attach point (ground-0.22+conduits.height*0.66, the exact formula `_build_pylons` already uses) to a point on the apparatus's own footprint: `apparatus.massing.grounding_base.radius` (3.4m) out from `apparatus.at`, toward whichever pylon is arriving, at half `apparatus.height` (4.2m) up from `apparatus.deck_y` (10.0) -- every number here is read off this file's own `apparatus`/`conduits` blocks above, not guessed.

cable_links._comment_sag_scale: FIX 1: was the literal `0.6` `tether_relay.gd::_build_cable_links` used to pass straight to `_conduit_span`'s `sag_scale` parameter. Span length here is roughly 4-6m (the 7-8m pylon-to-apparatus-centre distance this block's own comment already states, less the 3.4m `grounding_base.radius` the landing point sits at) -- at 0.6, sag = length * CONDUIT_SAG(0.05) * 0.6, about 0.15-0.2m over a 5-6m run: nearly a straight line, which is exactly the judge's 'unanchored debug line' read. 3.0 gives roughly 0.75-0.9m of droop over the same run, a real catenary sag at this scale. TUNABLE.
cable_links._comment_sockets: FIX 1: each span drawn from this block now lands on a small stone bracket + teal socket cap (`tether_relay.gd::_build_cable_socket`) built AT the landing point before the cable is drawn, so the cable terminates in something solid rather than the bare mid-air point `_comment_cable_links` above already documents. The bracket uses the same stone material every wall/deck on this site already carries; the cap shares the run's own lit-conduit material by identity, so it goes dark with the cable the moment `_kill_the_conduits()` fires.

_comment_deck_props: E-relay-dress: the raised apparatus pad -- the site's own 'work platform' -- was bare stone: a hero object and a console with nobody's kit anywhere near either. One compact cluster in the pad's south-east corner (local s~9.5-10.9, t~-6.1..-4.6), 4.7-5.1m from the apparatus centre (7,-9) so it clears the grounding base's 3.4m radius and its splayed feet with room to spare, and 6-8.9m from the console at (2.9,-9) so it never competes with that prompt. Placed at the pad's own absolute `deck_y` (10.0, the same value `decks[1].deck_y` authors) rather than sampled ground -- a prop dropped by ground height here would fall two-to-eight metres through the slab into the real terrain below it.

list._why: the cluster's anchor, in the pad's own south-east corner -- 1.6m off the s=12 edge, 1.4m off the t=-4 edge, 4.95m from the apparatus centre
touching the crate's own corner -- one load, not two, and the same 'touching pile reads as one' rule every ground-level cluster in this band already uses

the same worked-tool read the yard workstation already gives the ground level (props.json's `relay_station`), echoed up here so the platform itself shows somebody servicing the hardware, not just a stack of stock
leaned beside the whetstone, 1.2m from the crate -- the whole cluster spans under 2m across, one workstation rather than four separate objects

_comment_deck_people: FIX 2 (code-blind judge pass, this branch): 'counted three indistinct background figures... the grunts exist but are not in the shots that matter.' The site's three ground-level grunts (data/config/relay_site.json) stand on real sampled ground, which `village_npcs.gd::stand_at` can only ever ask the analytic heightfield for -- it has no way to seat a body on this deck's own absolute `deck_y`, the same limitation `deck_props`'s own header names for the crates up here. So the two figures that actually belong ON the raised pad (guarding the console, working the crate cluster) are built here instead, by `tether_relay.gd::_build_deck_people` -- real rigged, ranked, animated `npc_body.gd` bodies (the exact class `village_npcs.gd` uses), just seated by hand at `deck_y` the way `deck_props` seats crates, rather than by a ground raycast. `place_when`-equivalent is a build-time check against `relay_disabled` inside the builder itself (this file has no runtime flag-watch the way `village_npcs.gd`'s `place_when` does; a build-once check is consistent with everything else this file draws) -- a dead relay has nobody left posted on its own console.

list.name: Relay Console Guard
list._why: 2.0m north of the console (at [2.9,-9.0]) on the pad's own surface -- close enough to read as posted at it, clear of the console's own [1.6,1.15,0.9] box and its interaction radius. No `base` override (the plain `grunt` rig, per npc_ranks.json): the same body Relay Sentry already wears, but Sentry stands at the gate, off-frame from both the `standing` and `apparatus` stands, so there is no silhouette clash in either shot. Visible and UNoccluded by the apparatus's own 3.4m grounding-base radius from the `standing` eye (local [-8,-2], which approaches from the west/gantry side the console itself faces); the `apparatus` stand's own eye (local [14,-4], moved for FIX 3) looks from the opposite side, so this figure sits nearer the far edge of that frame rather than centred in it.

list.name: Relay Platform Hand
list._why: 1.9m from the deck crate cluster's own anchor crate (at [10.4,-5.4], `deck_props` above), facing it -- reads as tending the load rather than standing beside it by accident. 3.98m from the apparatus centre, clear of the 3.4m grounding-base radius. `base: grunt_a` (Relay Watch's own body) rather than the plain `grunt` Console Guard wears a few metres away in the same frame -- distinct silhouettes for two figures that ARE co-visible from both the `standing` and the (moved) `apparatus` stand. Nearest to camera and unoccluded by the apparatus bulk from the new `apparatus` eye (local [14,-4]): its own axis-distance from that eye is well short of the apparatus centre's, so it sits in the near ground rather than behind the object.

_comment_barrier: E-relay-dress: a barricade across the open road, 5.5m short of the gate piers (gate `at` s=-14, piers to s=-15.3) so it reads as a checkpoint held on the approach rather than crowding the gate's own open threshold -- the gate keeps its no-leaves design (`_comment_gate` above: Team Tether does not expect anyone to walk up this road), and this barrier is the thing that says otherwise before a visitor ever reaches it. A 3.4m gap at t -1.4..1.4 keeps the road itself walkable, the same 'line with a walked-through gap' grammar `relay_approach_checkpoint` already uses 400m up this same road (data/config/bands/band3_the_river_lock/props.json, order 3001) -- and deliberately asymmetric (crate+barrel west, one crate alone east) rather than mirrored, for the same reason that cluster's own round-4 note gives: a mirrored barricade reads as generated, not built.

list._why: west end of the line, squared close to the approach bearing so its face reads as blocking the road rather than sitting at an accident of an angle
set against the crate, one load closing the west end
east end, alone -- the asymmetry against the west end's pair is deliberate, not a missing piece

_comment_banner: E-relay-dress: staked at the barrier's own west end, the same 'staked, retinted Team Tether banner' grammar this band already repeats three times over (data/config/bands/band3_the_river_lock/props.json: `relay_approach_checkpoint`, `tether_haulage_wreck`, `crossing_watchpost`) -- the Medieval Castle kit's own Banner module (assets/buildings/quaternius_castle/Banner.obj, already installed, no new mesh), retinted the same oxblood #7a2430 through the identical `retint` mechanism `props.gd`/`building_prefabs.gd` already carry. A barricade of crates reads as an obstacle; a barricade with a staked banner over it reads as a claimed position.
_comment_dead_ground: D41, at full strength, and an HONEST PARTIAL, UPDATED AT OW5B. The authored source for the drain is terrain_playground.json's `drains.stations`, and `playground_heightfield.drain_factor()` is what every consumer asks. `scatter_rules.gd` thins vegetation at run time from that data directly, no bake dependency. The bake's colour/control maps are a THIRD consumer and were, as of OW5B (2026-08-17), re-baked with `drains.stations[4..6]` (the relay's three stations) in them -- but at the relay's PRE-relocation coordinates (108,34), because OW5B bakes landform only and does not move content. OW5D moves the relay's `site.centre` to (350,3760) in the SAME sitting, which strands that bake: the discoloured texture stays behind at the old, now-empty coordinates, and nothing paints the new site. So `enabled` STAYS TRUE here through OW5B and OW5C -- flipping it now would leave the relocated relay with no discolouration at all, on this bake or the runtime skin either. OW5D's own job, once it updates `drains.stations[4..6]`'s centres to (350,3760)-relative positions, is to re-bake ONLY the one region the new site falls in (region (0,7) at the 512m corridor pitch -- `build_playground_terrain.gd -- --regions=0:7`, seconds not hours, per OW5B's own per-region bake) and set `enabled` to false AS THE LAST STEP of that re-bake, once the baked texture actually agrees with the relay's shipped position. Same reasoning and same fix applies to the Old Quarry's `drains.stations[0..3]` at its own new region (0,3).

dead_ground._comment_heal_stations: CL-E12, and the owner's plain 'yes' to V-5 (docs/owner/OWNER_DIRECTIVES_2026-09-04.md, question 1). `heal_on_disable_seconds` below only fades THIS file's own runtime skin; it does not put back what the drain took out of the SCATTER, so before this the ground around the compound stayed bald after the console was pressed and the site read as half-healed. These are the relay's three entries in terrain_playground.json's `drains.stations` -- and exactly those three: the quarry's four have no console to press, which is the reason the contract's own question 1 asked about them separately and answered no. `tether_relay.gd::_heal_local_ground()` hands these ids to `meadow_healing.gd::heal_stations()`, which looks up their AUTHORED centres and radii (the same numbers `playground_heightfield.drain_factor()` reads and `scatter_rules._thin_by_drain` thinned on) and restores only the placements inside them. Everything else stays held for the chapter's own `legendary_freed` sweep. An empty list disables the vegetation half without touching the skin fade, and a name that is not a real station warns rather than failing silently -- a typo here is a site that quietly never heals, which is V-5's own *fails if*. WHAT STILL DOES NOT HEAL, per D45: the terrain's baked colour and control maps. Nothing at run time can repaint a texel, so the discolouration under the regrown plants survives; the plants, the skin and the dead lights are the three things that can change and all three do.
dead_ground._comment_heal_on_disable_seconds: GATE3_ENCOUNTER_CONTRACTS.md V-5, G3-BAND3-0903. D41: drained ground heals when the machinery fails. `meadow_healing.gd`'s own sweep only fires once, chapter-wide, on `legendary_freed` -- this is the earlier, filtered call `tether_relay.gd::disable_relay()` makes to its own already-existing `heal()` on THIS site's skin only, the moment its own console is pressed, so the crossing feels earned before the player has even reached it rather than waiting for the Warden. Same 12.0s fade `meadow_healing.json`'s own `dead_ground.fade_seconds` uses, so the relay does not fade faster or slower than the rest of the Meadows eventually will. 0 or less disables the early heal and leaves this site waiting for `legendary_freed` like every other station, without touching `meadow_healing.gd` itself.
dead_ground._comment_tint: ROUND8 MATERIAL DEFECT: was `#a89d84`, a pale warm grey (~RGB 168,157,132) chosen back when this skin drew directly over the RAW (bright, near-white) terrain -- see the old wording this replaces, below. `_build_ground_pad` now lays a real OPAQUE dark earth pad (`ground_pad.tint` #463c30, ~RGB 70,60,48) UNDER this skin across the whole compound floor, at a lower lift (0.03 vs this skin's 0.09), so `#a89d84` at `max_alpha` 0.72 was painting a pale sheet back over that pad and undoing it -- measured RGB(191,188,167) on `06-relay-road-day.png`, essentially unchanged from the pre-pad RGB(195.6,191.4,163.6). Old alpha-blend math: 0.72*(168,157,132) + 0.28*pad = ~(141,130,108) on channel R alone already above the 130 target. Fixed per option (a): darkened toward the pad's own family (`#584d3f`, ~RGB 88,77,63) and `max_alpha` cut from 0.72 to 0.4, so this skin now MODULATES the pad -- a subtle drain-driven darkening at the authored stations -- rather than replacing it. Expected composite at full alpha (assuming the pad's own composite reads close to its `ground_pad.tint` albedo, per that block's own header): 0.4*(88,77,63) + 0.6*(70,60,48) = ~RGB(77,68,54), a dark brown/grey well under the 130 target and nowhere near cream. TUNABLE, but keep it darker than or close to `ground_pad.tint` -- restoring a pale value here re-breaks this exact defect.
dead_ground._comment_lift: Metres above the sampled ground. Small enough not to read as a floating sheet, large enough that a 3m cell over 6-degree ground never lets the terrain poke through. Still above `ground_pad.lift` (0.03) so this skin draws visibly on top of the pad rather than z-fighting it.

_comment_ground_pad: ROUND7 MATERIAL DEFECT: the yard's own ground read bleached near-white (RGB 195.6,191.4,163.6 measured on `06-relay-road-day.png`) because the only thing painted over the real terrain there was `dead_ground` -- a translucent, UNTEXTURED vertex-colour wash (alpha capped at 0.72) with nothing solid under it, so up to 28% of the frame was always the raw (bright) terrain bleeding through, and the other 72% was a flat tint with no texture at all. `tether_relay.gd::_build_ground_pad` lays a real OPAQUE ground mesh first -- the same triplanar Ground030 dirt/pebble material `burrow_warrens.gd::_floor_material(true)` already wears for trodden approach ground, and the village `doorstep` prefab solves the same 'worked ground at a threshold' problem with the same idea (a real surface, not a colour wash) -- so the compound floor no longer depends on the terrain underneath it at all. `dead_ground`/`scorch_marks` (below) are UNCHANGED and still draw on top of this, now over dark packed earth instead of raw terrain, which is what they were always meant to weather. Authored in the site's own (s,t) frame like every other builder here, over a box a little larger than the wall footprint (walls run s -14..10, t -16..16) so the packed ground reads under the gate threshold and a couple of metres past the flanks rather than stopping exactly at the wall line.

ground_pad._comment_bounds: s -27..22 covers the road from just past the west_run's own outermost pylon (-26,-28's s) through the yard to past the apparatus pad (s=12 edge); t -19..19 clears both flank walls (t=+-16) by 3m so the packed ground has a worn verge rather than a hard-edged rectangle.
ground_pad._comment_lift: Beneath `dead_ground`'s own 0.09 lift, so that skin still paints visibly on TOP of this one rather than z-fighting it.
ground_pad._comment_tint: Packed dark earth/gravel -- close to `burrow_warrens.gd`'s own trodden-ground read (that file's `_apron_colour()` lerped toward `ROCK_TINT` at only 0.05, i.e. stays near its own dark source value) rather than the near-white the raw terrain bled through as. TUNABLE.
ground_pad._comment_wear: 'visible boot/tyre wear': a per-vertex darkening multiplier centred on t=0 -- the road/gantry axis every one of `relay_site.json`'s people and this file's own conduit runs already treat as the site's spine -- fading out over `wear_band_t` metres either side, so the worn track down the compound's own throughline reads darker than the ground either side of it. Procedural (vertex colour, computed from each sample's own t), no new texture.
